title: Exploring the Limits of LLMs as Quant Traders in Live Markets (Alpha Arena S1 tech post) + nof1 homepage
summary: nof1's own account of Season 1: six LLMs, $10k each on Hyperliquid perps, harness design, behaviour differences, and that fees from overtrading dominated early runs.

title: Alpha Arena Season 1 account totals and trades (archived API), rebuilt tables
summary: Hourly equity, positions and 515 trades rebuilt from archived API: returns +22% to -63%, 11-19x leverage, 4-8x exposure, 45-78% drawdowns, 21-30% win rates, fees up to 16.5% of capital, BTC flat.

title: HN: Exploring the limits of large language models as quant traders
summary: Discussion of Alpha Arena S1: models down 35% on average in 96 model-days, overbetting, need for constant-mix or random controls.

title: Grok 4.20 wins Alpha Arena Season 1.5 (US stocks)
summary: Season 1.5 (2025-11-19 to 12-03): eight models, four modes incl. 20x max leverage, US tech stocks; only Grok 4.20 profitable in aggregate (~+10-12%).

title: AI Bots Auditioning for Wall Street Trading Are Mostly Losing
summary: Round-up: only 6 of 32 Alpha Arena S1.5 runs profitable, combined portfolio lost about a third; bots overtrade; only 2 of 11 tracked arenas had a profitable median model.

title: AI-Trader: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in Real-Time Financial Markets
authors: Fan, Yang, Jiang, Zhang et al. (HKUDS)
summary: Live Oct-Nov 2025 benchmark of six LLMs on US stocks, A-shares and crypto with self-searched news; most agents weak, risk control decides cross-market robustness; no costs.

title: LiveTradeBench: Seeking Real-World Alpha with Large Language Models
summary: 50-day live test of 21 LLMs allocating across 15 US stocks and Polymarket; all positive on stocks in a rising market, LMArena score unrelated to returns; no costs, no buy-and-hold baseline.

title: StockBench: Can LLM Agents Trade Stocks Profitably In Real-world Markets?
authors: Chen, Yao, Liu, Xin et al.
summary: Mar-Jun 2025 backtest on 20 Dow stocks: best models +2% vs +0.4% buy-and-hold, all lag in downturns; news and fundamentals inputs matter; no costs.

title: When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents (Agent Market Arena)
authors: Qian, Peng, Wang, Zhang et al.
summary: Live Aug-Sep 2025 test of 4 agent designs x 5 LLMs on TSLA, BMRN, BTC, ETH; agent design matters more than the model; TradingAgents lost 38.7% on TSLA.

title: INVESTORBENCH: A Benchmark for Financial Decision-Making Tasks with LLM-based Agent
authors: Li, Cao, Yu, Javaji et al.
summary: 13 LLM backbones in a FinMem-style agent on stocks, crypto and ETFs; test windows (2020-2023) fall inside the models' training data.

title: FinBen: A Holistic Financial Benchmark for Large Language Models
authors: Xie, Han, Chen, Xiang et al.
summary: 36 datasets / 24 financial tasks; LLMs good at extraction and text analysis, weak at forecasting; trading task uses historical windows.

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
summary: Multi-agent LLM 'trading firm'; reports Sharpe 5.6-8.2 on AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN Jan-Mar 2024 with no costs; later reproductions with costs fall below buy-and-hold.

title: HN: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework (TradingAgents)
summary: Practitioner scepticism of TradingAgents: lagging inputs, code bugs (double-counted news, bullish-primed prompt), and a deterministic-risk + LLM-ranking alternative.

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
authors: Yu, Li, Chen, Jiang et al.
summary: LLM trading agent with layered memory and profile; strong short-window results that FINSABER shows do not generalise.

title: A Multimodal Foundation Agent for Financial Trading: Tool-Augmented, Diversified, and Generalist (FinAgent)
authors: Zhang, Zhao, Xia, Sun et al.
summary: Multimodal LLM agent (news, prices, charts) with reflection; claims 36% average profit improvement, 92% return on one dataset.

title: FinGPT: Open-Source Financial Large Language Models
summary: Open financial LLMs via data curation and LoRA; mainly sentiment and text tasks; no live trading evidence.

title: FinRobot: An Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Financial Applications using Large Language Models
summary: LLM agent platform aimed at equity research and valuation, not trading.

title: Can LLM-based Financial Investing Strategies Outperform the Market in Long Run? (FINSABER)
summary: 2004-2024 re-test of FinMem and FinAgent on ~100 symbols with costs: both lose to buy-and-hold, no significant alpha; too cautious in bulls, too aggressive in bears.

title: Profit Mirage: Revisiting Information Leakage in LLM-based Financial Agents
authors: Li, Zeng, Xing, Xu et al.
summary: Five LLM agents lose 51-62% of Sharpe after the knowledge cutoff; 69-82% of decisions unchanged when inputs are perturbed; recommends LLMs as strategy generators.

title: The Memorization Problem: Can We Trust LLMs' Economic Forecasts?
summary: GPT-4o recalls index levels (0.6% error) and directions before its cutoff but not after; instructions and masking do not prevent recall; evaluate only post-cutoff.

title: The Alpha Illusion: Reported Alpha from LLM Trading Agents Should Not Be Treated as Deployment Evidence
authors: Ye, Han, Hu, Bu et al.
summary: Position paper: 35 of 40 cost components unmodelled in top LLM agents; 2025 reproduction with costs puts TradingAgents and QuantAgent below buy-and-hold; proposes P1-P6 protocols and a modular design.

title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models
summary: Post-cutoff GPT-4 headline scores predict 1-2 day drift (Sharpe 2.97, strongest in small caps and negative news); Sharpe decayed 6.5 to 1.2 by 2024; unprofitable at 20 bp round trip.

title: DatedGPT: Preventing Lookahead Bias in Large Language Models with Time-Aware Pretraining
summary: Twelve 1.3B LLMs with annual cutoffs 2013-2024; measures a lookahead premium in news-based return prediction; a route to honest LLM backtests.

title: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
authors: Shi, Fu, Chen, Zhao et al.
summary: Candlestick foundation model on 12B+ bars from 45 exchanges; authors report better RankIC and volatility MAE than TSFMs and GARCH, A-share backtest IR 1.65; open 4M-102M models (MIT).

title: GitHub repos: TimesFM (2.5/3.0 release notes, weights licence), Kronos, AI-Trader, TradingAgents and others
summary: Repo facts as of 2026-10-13: TimesFM 3.0 adds multivariate/covariates but weights are non-commercial; Kronos model sizes and context; stars and licences.

title: Re(Visiting) Time Series Foundation Models in Finance
summary: Zero-shot and fine-tuned TSFMs (TimesFM, Chronos, Moirai, Lag-Llama ...) fail on daily excess returns (~50% direction, negative R2); finance-pretrained models do better; all strategies negative at 20 bp.

title: Forecasting Realized Volatility with Time Series Foundation Models: A Comparison with Econometric Benchmarks
summary: Nine zero-shot TSFMs vs HAR on 50 assets: only tiny TTM beats log-HAR; TimesFM 2.5 needs recalibration; averaging a TSFM with log-HAR is the robust choice.

title: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models for Financial Return Forecasting
summary: TimeGPT, TimesFM-2.5, Moirai-2.0, Chronos(-2) vs trained baselines on 5 US stocks 2024-26: TSFMs rank best but rarely beat a random walk.

title: FinRL: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Library for Automated Stock Trading in Quantitative Finance
authors: Liu, Yang, Chen, Zhang et al.
summary: The standard open deep-RL trading library (PPO, SAC, DDPG ...) with stock environments and tutorials.

title: FinRL Contests: Benchmarking Data-driven Financial Reinforcement Learning Agents
authors: Wang, Holzer, Xia, Cao et al.
summary: Summary of 2023-2025 contests: winning stock-trading teams beat the Dow on Sharpe/drawdown but not on return in short live tests; generalisation remains the problem.

title: LOB-Based Deep Learning Models for Stock Price Trend Prediction: A Benchmark Study (LOBCAST)
authors: Prata, Masi, Berti, Arrigoni et al.
summary: 15 order-book deep models re-run: F1 drops from ~83 to ~60 on new data, published claims not reproduced, no after-cost profitability.

title: Optiver - Trading at the Close: 1st place solution
summary: CatBoost+GRU+Transformer on 300 features; online retraining every 12 days and index-relative post-processing were key; time-series validation.

title: Jane Street Real-Time Market Data Forecasting: 8th place solution, lessons thread, 2nd place reproduction
summary: Small GRUs with one gradient step per new label; online learning was the biggest gain (+0.005 to +0.008 R2 on scores of ~0.01-0.02).

title: G-Research Crypto Forecasting: wrap-up, 2nd and 3rd place solutions, leak thread
summary: 15-min crypto returns: winners used single LightGBMs, walk-forward CV, market-relative features; true scores ~0.02 correlation; public leaderboard leaked.

title: Jane Street Market Prediction: 1st place (supervised autoencoder + MLP)
summary: Purged gapped time-series CV and training the autoencoder inside each fold to avoid label leakage.

title: Downside Risk Reduction Using Regime-Switching Signals: A Statistical Jump Model Approach
summary: 2-state jump model on downside deviation and Sortino features; 1990-2023 with 10 bp costs and 1-day delay: S&P 500 Sharpe 0.48 to 0.68, max drawdown 55% to 27%.

title: Factor Momentum Everywhere
summary: 65 equity factors show time-series momentum (monthly AR(1) ~0.11, positive for 59); supports trusting strategies with good recent records, modestly.
